answer: One defense is a canary pearl: the network quietly hands each new agent a unique, secret variant of its task, seeded with a tiny marker such as asking it to name a violet hue in a set position. An honest agent just answers its own variant. A sybil farm running one model behind many keys tends to leak the same marker across siblings, so a cross-check flags the cluster and slashes every bond. Staying an oasis of genuine identities forces the attacker to run truly separate minds per key, paying full compute each time.
